title: Thursday Teacher Plan
note: Turn-in day for all grades (no class Fri Nov 20). 8th has a guest teacher: video + questions + links. 7th and 6th as planned.

4th Period.topic: How Electricity Works (video) + turn in the week (guest teacher)
4th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can explain what volts, amps, and ohms mean using the video, and my week's circuit links are turned in once.
4th Period.exitTicket: None today: the Answers tab is the one turn-in.
prep: Blooket: 8th_Thu_Nov19_Blooket_Dial (host link needed; skip if it won't run)
8th_Thu_Nov19_Electricity_Video_TurnIn: move the Answers pages into Tab 2, attach as a copy per student

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Host 8th_Thu_Nov19_Blooket_Dial.
segments.why: Spiral review of Wednesday (taught by the sub).
tips: Watch for the most-missed question: Wednesday was a sub day, so expect gaps.

segments.title: Today's goal + how it's graded
segments.do: Read the goal and the points table; say: watch only to 8:25, turn in once at the end.
segments.why: Clear target and one turn-in (Maslow).

segments.title: Watch: 0:00 to 8:25
segments.do: Students watch individually with subtitles on, pausing at each timestamp.
segments.why: Input before output; subtitles support ELs and dyslexic learners.
tips: Stop at 8:25: the rest (surface charge, EM waves) is beyond 8th grade and is Future Engineer.

segments.title: Answer: Part 1, the video
segments.do: Students answer 6 questions in Tab 2 with frames.
segments.why: Recall and explain (Bloom: Remember/Understand).
tips: Key 1: light, heat, motion, magnetic fields, electric arcs (any 2).
Key 2: electrons; negative terminal to positive terminal.
Key 3: the beam was negative particles (electrons) moving negative to positive, so electricity really flows − to +.
Key 4: volts = push/pressure, amps = flow/current, ohms = resistance.
Key 5: the 220 Ω resistor, so too much current doesn't burn out the LED.
Key 6: copper has 1 free electron in its outer (valence) shell that can move to other atoms.

segments.title: Part 2: paste your circuit links
segments.do: Students paste Blink, Button, Dial links; build any missing one from that day's handout.
segments.why: Collects the week's work in one turn-in.
tips: Input answer: Button (input: button, output: LED) or Dial (input: potentiometer, output: LED).

segments.title: Final check + turn in once
segments.do: Checklist, then Turn in.
segments.why: One turn-in.

watchFor: Students watching past 8:25 and getting lost
Answers pasted from the transcript instead of their own words

6th Period.topic: Cam and Follower: label, screenshot, turn in
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my cam and follower are finished, labeled, and turned in once.
6th Period.exitTicket: None today: the Answers tab is the one turn-in.
prep: 7th_Thu_Nov19_Cam_TurnIn: move the Answers page into Tab 2, attach as a copy per student

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Host 7th_Thu_Nov19_Blooket_Follower.
segments.why: Spiral review of Wednesday (taught by the sub).
tips: Watch for the most-missed question: Wednesday was a sub day, so expect gaps.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Re-teach the most-missed question, read the goal, and say clearly: turn in once, at the end of today.
segments.why: Students know the target and the one turn-in (Maslow).
tips: Likely most-missed: Shift + arrow moves 10 mm.

segments.title: Label: cam, follower, axle
segments.do: Text shapes CAM / FOLLOWER / AXLE next to each part; color cam orange, follower purple, axle blue.
segments.why: Precise vocabulary attached to the model (ELD).
tips: Students missing the follower: Wednesday's steps first (Box 6×40×10, Align, Shift + up ×4).

segments.title: Screenshot + share link
segments.do: TOP view, Ctrl + Shift + Show windows screenshot, Share, copy link, test it.
segments.why: Evidence for the turn-in.
tips: If Share's options look different, have them copy whichever link the Share window gives.

segments.title: Fill in the Answers tab
segments.do: Paste screenshot and link, write 2 sentences with the frames.
segments.why: Explain the mechanism (Bloom: Understand).
tips: Model answer: when the cam spins, the off-center side pushes the follower up, then lets it drop, so spinning turns into up-and-down motion.

segments.title: Gallery walk: 2 classmates
segments.do: Look at 2 classmates' screens and give one specific compliment each.
segments.why: Peer recognition (PBL public product; Complex Instruction status).

segments.title: Turn in once
segments.do: Checklist, then Turn in on Google Classroom.
segments.why: One turn-in.

watchFor: Students who never finished Tuesday's cam

7th Period.topic: Tensegrity: build day + turn in (first build of the week)
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, my pair has built a tensegrity, tried to make it stand on its own, and turned in a photo once.
7th Period.exitTicket: None today: the Answers tab is the one turn-in.
prep: 6th_Thu_Nov19_Tensegrity_Build_TurnIn printed (4 pages) + Answers tab as a Google Doc copy per student
Per pair: 3 popsicle sticks, string, scissors, pencil (students cut their own string)
Your own sticks + string to model

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Host 6th_Thu_Nov19_Blooket_NetForce.
segments.why: Spiral review of Wednesday (taught by the sub).
tips: Watch for the most-missed question: Wednesday was a sub day, so expect gaps.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Re-teach the most-missed question, read the goal, and say clearly: turn in once, at the end of today.
segments.why: Students know the target and the one turn-in (Maslow).
tips: Likely most-missed: the 3-force puzzle (40 + 30 − 50 = 20 N right).

segments.title: Roles by birthday + I do: tie the first string
segments.do: Pairs line up by birthday (younger = Holder, older = Tier). Model: label A/B/C, dot the tops, cut 2 sticks long, wrap twice, knot + bow, tie A bottom to B bottom.
segments.why: Worked round first; roles with real jobs (Complex Instruction).
tips: The bow lets them retie when tightening.

segments.title: You do: tie the frame
segments.do: Pairs finish the 9 strings from the tie map, swapping roles after the bottom triangle.
segments.why: Hands-on Create; the 9-step map is real rigor for a class that wants challenge.
tips: Check: 3 strings on every stick end; no stick touching another.
Pairs behind at minute 15: help them finish the cross strings first.

segments.title: Tighten until it stands
segments.do: Shorten all 3 cross strings by the same amount, a finger-width at a time, until it stands without sticks touching.
segments.why: Iterate and test (MS-ETS1-4).
tips: Leaning = that side's cross string is loose. Sticks touching = triangles too tight.
Standing isn't required for credit; what they changed is.

segments.title: Photo + Answers tab
segments.do: Photo with the Chromebook camera; answer tension/compression + what they changed.
segments.why: Connects the build to the week's force ideas (Bloom: Evaluate).
tips: Answer key: strings are in tension (they pull); sticks are in compression (they're squeezed/push).

segments.title: Turn in once
segments.do: Each partner turns in their own copy once.
segments.why: One turn-in.

watchFor: Pairs where one partner does everything: enforce the swap
Clean-up of string scraps before the bell

accommodations: Goal read after the Blooket, numbered steps, worked first round, checklists, sentence frames in every Answers tab, frequent check-ins.
Key words with diagrams, frames for every answer, partner talk before writing.
Lexend Deca, steps read aloud, speech-to-text OK for Answers tabs, spelling not graded.
Short timed chunks, hands-on roles in 6th, visual timer, break pass.
Extended time to Sunday, dictated answers, intentional partners. Floors: 8th turns in the links they have + 1 sentence; 7th screenshot + link; 6th photo of the frame (standing optional) + 1 answer.
Future Engineer (OPTIONAL) box in each Answers tab: 1 KB point.
frameworks: Every grade ends the week with one product: 4 circuit links, a labeled TinkerCAD cam, a built tensegrity photo.
Birthday roles with a required swap (6th); gallery walk compliments (7th); publicly assign competence.
Welcome back after two sub days, one turn-in, 'you are not behind', missing pieces still accepted.
Apply/Create (build) into Evaluate (explain, input vs output, tension vs compression).
